SMTO-TSK-0051 — SMTO couldn't confirm that your Stop request worked

GUID: 8335d4ed-f283-4119-b422-6a40cad432e7
Slug: stop-persistence-failed
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • You selected Stop, but SMTO couldn't confirm the result. The task may already be stopping, or it may still be running, so check before doing anything else.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few seconds, then look at the task in the conversation and see whether it shows as stopped or stopping. SMTO may have stopped the task even though it couldn't confirm it to you.
  2. Reload the SMTO page if the task's status doesn't seem to change. Reloading shows the task's real current status instead of what the page last saw.
  3. Only if the task is still running, select Stop again. If it shows Force stop, select that. A second Stop is only needed when the first one did not take effect.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as stopped and no new steps appear under it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they can check the server's log for why Stop failed. Don't assume the task finished or that it stopped; check what it already did before asking for the same work again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • RunCancellationCoordinator.stop raised during Stop processing (durable commit, publication or cleanup), so the Stop route returned a failure; when a local cancel event existed it was set as an emergency freeze.

What this means

  • The cancellation coordinator raised an exception anywhere in Stop processing, potentially during persistence or later publication/cleanup; an available local event is set as an emergency freeze. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The cancellation coordinator raised an exception anywhere in Stop processing, potentially during persistence or later publication/cleanup; an available local event is set as an emergency freeze.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect durable cancellation, current owners and any publication failure; this exception alone does not prove the Stop record was never saved.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the run's current status and cancellation record (task status in the UI, or the run's events in the current-run store) before acting; the local cancel event may already have frozen work even though the durable Stop was not confirmed. Request Stop again only if the run is still active, and check the Server log for the exception raised by RunCancellationCoordinator.stop.
  • Refresh authoritative task/cancellation state and use Stop again only if still needed; do not assume either continued execution or completed shutdown from this error alone.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative state confirms the Stop decision and existing work settles through its owner.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
